findings.title: A slow restore replaces a different project opened afterward — restore applies its response without an identity guard
findings.surface: Compare → Restore vN while opening another project
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: an owner/editor restoring project A can open project B while the request is slow. The late A response switches the workspace back to A and clears B's unsynthesized inputs via openSystem, without confirmation. B's saved copy remains recoverable by reopening it, but edits made during that interval are lost. The source proves the overwrite branch; no network timing was executed.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:455 awaits restore for the current project, but :458-459 unconditionally setProject(meta) and openSystem(system, context). Unlike save's identity check at :345,353 and synthesis's check at :237,243, restore never checks projectRef or a request identity. Project buttons remain active at ProjectsPanel.jsx:95 during restore.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: preserve "context restoration ... return paths". Restoring A should not replace a different project opened while A's request was pending.
reproduction_steps: Open project A → Compare → select v1 → Restore v1.
While its request is pending, open B from Projects and type a synthesis note or adjust dials.
When A's response arrives, source predicts A replaces B and B's queued edits disappear.

findings.title: Old checkpoints become unreachable after 1,000 saves — version history is silently truncated
findings.surface: Compare saved-version selector and History modal; GET /api/projects/{id}/versions
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: at version 1001, v1 disappears from Compare and History although it remains stored. Developers with long-lived projects cannot find, label, compare, or restore that older checkpoint through the offered UI; there is no Load more or indication of missing rows. Newer history remains usable, so the impairment is limited to older versions after this growth threshold.
findings.evidence: projects.py:215 sorts descending and calls to_list(1000) with no pagination or truncation metadata; Workspace.jsx:478-479 puts only that array into versions; :522-523 and HistoryModal.jsx:9 render that array as all saved versions. Version detail requires a number and the UI offers no separate arbitrary-version lookup.
findings.expected: R-190: "history listing every saved version with its note, saver and time"; R-176: roll back to "any saved version"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation".
reproduction_steps: Use a project with 1001 successful saved snapshots.
Open Compare → History or the compare-against menu.
Source predicts only v1001 through v2, with no pagination to v1 or warning that history is incomplete.

findings.title: Valid indented C++ implementations are reported as missing — definition scanning rejects leading whitespace
findings.surface: C++ → instant Compile check; export-check dialog
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: a correctly declared Heal UFUNCTION whose legal .cpp definition begins with spaces is omitted from the definition set and falsely reported as a linker error. Identical code without indentation is accepted. Developers are instructed to implement functions that already exist and may spend time regenerating valid code; Export anyway remains a safe workaround. No Unreal compile was run.
findings.evidence: compileCheck.js:102 anchors definitions with /^(?![ \t#]).../gm, explicitly excluding leading space/tab. :104 builds defined solely from these matches; :122 reports every UFUNCTION absent from that set as never defined, and :128 applies it to replication.
findings.expected: R-192 requires flagging actual likely mistakes, R-199: "For a C++ pair with no likely mistakes ... 'No likely mistakes found'". Checklist, logic-precision/business logic: use the language contract as oracle—leading indentation before a top-level C++ definition does not change whether the function is defined.
reproduction_steps: Open/import a valid UHealthComponent with UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) void Heal(); in its header.
Have its .cpp include the matching header and define the method as an indented top-level definition, e.g. four spaces before void UHealthComponent::Heal() {}.
Open C++: the source predicts Heal is reported as never defined. Remove only leading spaces and the false issue disappears.

findings.title: The daily counter and first synthesis warning retain yesterday's usage — usage refreshes only after local actions
findings.surface: Usage chip; near-limit warning on Synthesize
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: an open workspace at 450 requests keeps displaying 450 / ~500 today after midnight Pacific until a local request or reload refreshes usage. Pressing Synthesize first uses yesterday's 450 and shows a near-limit warning for a fresh day. Reload is a safe workaround, but the counter and warning misrepresent current quota. Another tab's calls similarly leave this tab's count stale; the midnight witness does not require concurrency.
findings.evidence: UsageChip.jsx:12-20 fetches only when aiKey or refreshKey changes; there is no midnight timer, day comparison, focus refresh or cross-tab usage event. Workspace.jsx:183 supplies usageTick, incremented on this tab's completed actions (:261,953-954), not passage of time. :226-233 consumes that same stale data for the warning. Backend server.py:40-41,497-505 correctly reads the current Pacific day when queried.
findings.expected: R-174: count is requests used "today" and resets at midnight Pacific; R-198 requires accurate zero/one/limit states. R-205's server day boundary is implemented, but the visible counter must refresh to display the new day's zero. For example 23:59:59 and 00:00:01 Pacific belong to different days independently of local timezone.
reproduction_steps: Keep a workspace open with 450 Flash-Lite requests recorded just before midnight Pacific.
Leave it open past midnight without changing key settings or making a request.
Source predicts the chip still reads 450 / ~500 today; pressing Synthesize warns using that old count even though the server's new day is empty.
Reload to obtain the correct zero.

findings.title: Export ignores problems already found by AI review — review results never reach the export warning state
findings.surface: AI review → UE5 .zip → either export format
findings.observed: AI and model features: if the instant checker is clean but AI review reports a genuine signature/API error, clicking either zip option downloads directly without showing the known AI issues. Switching away from C++ unmounts and loses the review as well. Developers can miss warnings they paid to obtain just before exporting; they can still manually read and act on the C++ panel, so this is a bounded integration failure rather than evidence of actual generated-code correctness.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:559 creates checkIssues from checkSystem(result) only; exportZip at :439 guards only checkIssues.length. CompileCheck.jsx:32 stores AI review in child-local ai state, :46 sets it, :81 renders its issues; no callback passes those issues to the workspace (props at Workspace.jsx:807 only include onUsed/onNeedKey). PublicView.jsx:45-46 bypasses checks entirely.
findings.expected: Request: "Compile Check: Flag likely C++ mistakes ... before you export" and "Built-in check plus AI review"; R-196: "When the compile check found any issue ... opens an export-check dialog listing the issues" while still permitting Export anyway.
reproduction_steps: Open a system for which the built-in check reports no likely mistakes.
Run AI review; condition: it returns a valid nonempty issue list.
Choose UE5 .zip → Unreal plugin or Source files only.
Source predicts immediate download without the requested warning listing those known issues.

findings.title: Keyboard focus escapes the new dialogs and leaves background actions active — shared Modal has no focus management
findings.surface: New bundle, history, save, limit-warning and export-check dialogs via shared Modal
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: keyboard users opening Bundle plugin, History, or export warnings keep focus on the triggering background control. Tab traverses the workspace rather than entering a confined dialog, and can leave even the Save dialog after its last control. Background actions remain operable under the visual backdrop, making accidental project changes and finding the actual confirmation controls possible only through a long traversal. Escape remains a safe close path; this is a meaningful accessibility impairment, not a measured visual issue.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 registers only Escape; :11-12 renders a backdrop and role=dialog aria-modal=true, without focus placement/trap, inert background, or restore-focus cleanup. BundleModal.jsx:51 has no autoFocus; the new history/export dialogs have no focus setup either. Workspace.jsx:975-1008 mounts these dialogs over still-enabled workspace controls.
findings.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and dialogs preserve the "focus/background interaction contract". A modal marked aria-modal must put keyboard interaction inside it and return focus when closed.
reproduction_steps: Use the keyboard to focus Bundle plugin or History and press Enter.
Press Tab and Shift+Tab.
Source predicts focus follows underlying document order without confinement to the open modal.
Close the modal: no restore-focus logic returns focus to its trigger.

findings.title: Bundles omit dependencies used only through sibling headers or delegates — dependency planning matches class names rather than includes
findings.surface: Projects → Bundle plugin → sibling module dependency planning
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: suppose Health's header declares UHealthComponent and FOnHealthChanged via a delegate macro, and Stamina includes HealthComponent.h but uses only FOnHealthChanged. The bundler never recognizes that as using HealthKit, so StaminaKit.Build.cs lacks HealthKit and Unreal cannot resolve the sibling public header on its module include path. Bundling valid interoperating systems therefore requires manual Build.cs edits. This is a source-predicted dependency omission; no exported plugin was compiled.
findings.evidence: zipExport.js:13-15 extracts only class/struct identifiers; :225 adds sibling dependencies only when such an identifier appears in the consumer code. It does not inspect sibling #include paths or DECLARE_*DELEGATE names. :254 passes only p.uses to writeModule, which writes those dependencies at :164-167.
findings.expected: R-187: "copying the folder ... installs every selected system together"; R-208: required engine dependencies and request: "with its own module files, so it installs with no code edits"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace structure and dependencies through to usable output. A consumer that includes a sibling module's public header needs that sibling in Build.cs, even if it uses only a delegate declared there.
reproduction_steps: Have a Health project with HealthComponent.generated.h, UHealthComponent and a macro-declared FOnHealthChanged delegate.
Have a Stamina project whose code includes HealthComponent.h and uses FOnHealthChanged without referencing UHealthComponent.
Bundle both projects and inspect StaminaKit.Build.cs.
HealthKit is absent; add it manually to make the sibling public include available.

findings.title: A successful concurrent save can report failure — backfill and post-save snapshot inserts race on the same version
findings.surface: Save project; PUT /api/projects/{project_id}; version history
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source-predicted interleaving: A commits v2 and pauses before line 195; B loads v2, finds its snapshot missing and backfills v2 at line 180; A's line 195 now raises duplicate-key and returns 500 although A's content is already saved. A sees 'Couldn't save', retains the stale base version and must reopen or resolve a spurious conflict. This affects simultaneous team saves and miscommunicates a committed operation; the atomic project update itself prevents silent content overwriting.
findings.evidence: backend/projects.py:178-182 checks for a missing current snapshot and inserts it, swallowing exceptions; :184-188 atomically updates the project/version; :195 then unconditionally inserts that new version snapshot. server.py:54 declares (project_id, version) unique. Workspace.jsx:307-308 treats a non-409 error as 'Couldn't save' and leaves its old version metadata.
findings.expected: R-156: 'Every project create and every successful save writes an immutable snapshot'; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: 'Identify commit points ... inspect ... completion recording ... and communicated uncertainty.' Saving and recording a version must not race into reporting a committed save as rejected.
reproduction_steps: Open the same project in two editor sessions.
Have editor A save v1 to v2; before its snapshot insert completes, let editor B load v2 and save.
B backfills the missing v2 snapshot; A's unconditional v2 insert violates the unique index.
A receives 'Couldn't save' even though its v2 write committed.

findings.title: Long-lived projects lose access to older comparisons — version lists silently stop at 1,000 snapshots
findings.surface: Compare base selector; GET /api/projects/{id}/versions
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after a team makes 1,001 saved versions, v1 is still stored but is absent from the only version list and Compare selector. More saves push further earlier versions out. The user cannot select those versions through the app; there is no pagination or truncation notice. This is a bounded history-access failure, recoverable only through a caller knowing the omitted version number, not through the UI.
findings.evidence: backend/projects.py:203-205 sorts versions descending and calls '.to_list(1000)' without an offset, cursor or total; Workspace.jsx:388 uses that single response and :408-411 renders only those returned versions.
findings.expected: request: 'Keep every saved version of a project so Compare works against any earlier one, not just the last'; R-156: 'lists every snapshot newest first'; R-157: 'every saved version of the open project'. All retained versions must be reachable, with pagination if needed.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate 1,001 saves on a project.
Reopen it and open Compare.
Open 'Compare against': only v1001 through v2 are returned; v1 is unavailable.

findings.title: Paid users with exhausted credits are told their model requires a paid key — all insufficient-quota errors are classified as free-tier refusals
findings.surface: AI key window Test key/Save; synthesis error banner
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: for an OpenAI account that already has a paid key but has exhausted its balance or spending quota, the provider's insufficient_quota response is converted into a false free-tier diagnosis. Settings blocks saving that model and offers Gemini instead of explaining credit/quota recovery. Users lose the correct cause and perform needless key/model changes; no unauthorized billing or actual provider response was observed.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:280-281 maps any 'insufficient_quota' exception to paid_model_required and the message at :33 asserts 'this key is on the free tier'; AiKeyModal.jsx:109-111 refuses Save for this code and :161-165 renders the paid-key error; Workspace.jsx:222,634-641 renders the switch-model recovery.
findings.expected: R-105: failures show 'a message in plain English naming that cause'; R-154 distinguishes 'an exhausted free quota' from 'a model that needs a paid key'; R-163 limits paid_model_required to a key 'the provider reports as free-tier'. Insufficient quota alone does not establish the logical condition that a model excludes the key's tier; report quota exhaustion without asserting free-tier status.
reproduction_steps: Use an OpenAI key whose account has exhausted its credits or spend limit.
Select GPT-4.1 and press Test key.
When the provider reports insufficient_quota, the app says the key is free-tier and blocks saving with a paid-key error.

findings.title: Stacking discards the saved implementations before asking the AI to merge — only metadata and a header excerpt reach the provider
findings.surface: Projects > Stack N systems
findings.observed: AI and model features: choose two saved projects whose summaries/headers are similar but whose .cpp contains distinct game logic. Neither implementation is sent to the selected provider. The merge cannot ground its result in either actual implementation and may replace existing behavior with invented logic. This is a source-proven omission, not an assertion about a specific unexecuted model reply. Users can still generate a new combined architecture, but cannot rely on Stack to build on their saved code.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:252 retrieves full saved systems, then :263 calls systems.map(compactForApi). changes.js:75-83 returns only name, summary, module flags, parameters, network notes and the first 4,000 header characters; it omits cpp_source, pseudocode and setup. server.py:248 calls compact_system(s,4000) with full=False, so its model prompt also lacks all implementations.
findings.expected: request: 'Stack Systems ... keep working with cloud projects' and teams 'build on the same systems'; R-155 calls for 'one merged system'; checklist, AI and model features: 'Compare the promised task with the actual ... source records ... transformations, truncation ... that could remove essential meaning.' A code merge must receive the implementation it is meant to preserve and integrate.
reproduction_steps: Save two generated systems with important behavior implemented in cpp_source rather than their short summaries.
Select both in Projects and click Stack 2 systems.
Trace the posted stack_systems and provider prompt: neither contains cpp_source or the setup/pseudocode bodies.

findings.title: Regenerating a longer saved system loses the tail of its code context — the backend still truncates the supposedly full previous implementation
findings.surface: Synthesize / Regenerate with N changes
findings.observed: AI and model features: a valid saved/imported project with a .cpp longer than 12,000 characters can be reopened and regenerated, but code after that boundary never reaches the model. A queued unrelated parameter change therefore has no grounding for preserving tail-only behavior. The accepted project schema has no matching size limit or warning. This predicts omitted revision context rather than claiming a particular generated code loss was executed; users must manually reconcile long implementations.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:245 now sends the full result as previous_system, but server.py:251 calls compact_system(...,8000,full=True); :227 cuts the header to 8,000 characters, :230 cuts the source to 12,000 and :231 cuts pseudocode to 6,000. SYSTEM_PROMPT at :192 promises to keep everything unaffected.
findings.expected: request: teams should 'build on the same systems'; R-169 requires previous inputs map into the complete system; checklist, AI and model features: inspect 'transformations, truncation ... that could remove essential meaning'. The exposed revision contract at server.py:192 is 'Keep everything ... not affected'; the full implementation must reach that revision or the user must be warned/refused before it is silently omitted.
reproduction_steps: Import/open a valid project with a cpp_source over 12,000 characters and a meaningful function at the end.
Queue a dial or parameter change and regenerate.
Inspect the source path: only cpp_source[:12000] is used in the provider prompt, despite the full previous_system sent by the browser.

findings.title: Linking a normal email account to Google disables its existing email sign-in — every unverified password is deleted without a replacement flow
findings.surface: Email/password sign-in after Continue with Google
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a legitimate developer signs up with a password, later uses Google with the same email, then finds the original password permanently rejected. This new security fix treats all unverified email signups as hostile and offers no user-controlled password re-enrollment; Google still opens the same projects, but password sign-in now requires owner intervention. This is bounded loss of one explicitly supported sign-in method, not loss of the entire account.
findings.evidence: auth.py:135-137 creates every ordinary password account with email_verified=False. First Google sign-in for that address enters :175, unconditionally $unset password_hash at :177, and persists it at :180. login at :152 refuses users without password_hash; register at :132-133 refuses the existing email. Forgot password at Login.jsx:83-84 sends the user to the owner for a reset link.
findings.expected: request: 'Two ways to sign in: Google, or email and password. If both use the same email address, they reach the same account.' Prevent pre-registration takeover while letting the verified owner retain or securely re-establish the promised email/password method, rather than silently deleting it.
reproduction_steps: Create an email/password account and save a project.
Sign out, then Continue with Google using that email.
Sign out and try the original email/password.
It is rejected; signup with the same email is also refused, leaving Google or an owner-issued reset as the only recovery.

findings.title: Keyboard focus stays in the covered workspace when key settings opens — the dialog lacks focus management and trapping
findings.surface: Your AI key modal (shared Modal)
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: opening Your AI key leaves focus on the covered trigger and permits tabbing through/activating the background workspace before reaching modal fields at the end of the DOM. The visible modal is announced as modal without modal keyboard behavior. Keyboard users incur substantial extra navigation and can accidentally act on obscured controls; the dialog remains reachable by tabbing, so this is not an absolute keyboard exclusion.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 adds only an Escape listener; :11 draws a backdrop; :12 adds aria-modal=true but implements no focus move, Tab trapping, inert background or focus restoration. AiKeyModal.jsx:126 uses this shared Modal. Workspace.jsx:535-539 leaves Synthesize enabled beneath it when no generation is running.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: 'keyboard focus ... follows the active surface' and 'an editor overlay must preserve the supported focus/background interaction contract'. Opening Your AI key must put keyboard users in the dialog, keep focus there and restore it on close.
reproduction_steps: Focus Add AI key with the keyboard and activate it.
Press Tab repeatedly.
Focus continues through the covered workspace rather than moving to provider/model/key controls and staying inside the dialog.
Close with Escape: there is no explicit focus restoration.

findings.title: Partial model results are reported as complete systems — validation permits empty sections and blank setup instructions
findings.surface: Generation job completion; parameters/modules/Event Graph/Setup Guide
findings.observed: AI and model features: a parseable provider response with nonempty code/pseudocode and one graph node/setup item but modules=[], tunable_parameters=[], node_graph_edges=[] and blank setup text is marked done. The workspace shows no parameter sliders, no actual module list, a disconnected graph and blank setup instructions as a finished system. This is a conditional source prediction for a partial provider reply, not an observed generation; users must spend another generation to recover missing output.
findings.evidence: SystemOutput at server.py:146-147,151-154 accepts empty lists for parameters/modules/setup/nodes/edges. The extra checks at :345-347 reject only empty strings for four fields, empty nodes and empty setup. Empty modules, parameters or edges pass; setup entries with blank title/detail pass SetupStep at :129-133; :352 then stores status='done'.
findings.expected: R-169: a reply 'missing the system sections fails the job instead of producing a blank or partial system'; checklist, AI and model features: 'Follow ... semantic validation ... against the ... field/format ... contract.' Accepted results must contain usable promised sections, not merely correctly typed empty arrays/steps.
reproduction_steps: Run a synthesis whose provider reply parses but contains empty modules, parameters and edges and a setup step with an empty title/detail.
Follow SystemOutput validation and the missing-fields check.
The job is stored as done and the partial system is displayed instead of an incomplete-output failure.

findings.title: Compare can show another project's baseline after switching — version fetches apply stale responses without an identity check
findings.surface: Compare > Compare against; switching projects during a version fetch
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: select A's saved v1, switch to B before its detail request returns, then receive A's response. It installs A's baseline after the B-change reset; Compare now shows A's code as 'v1' against B and can offer B's version selector with that same number selected. Out-of-order selections within one project can likewise revert the user's latest choice. The user receives a misleading comparison and must reselect the version to recover; both projects are authorized, so this is not a data-access claim.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:388 stores any version-list response without checking project identity; :391 resets base on project changes, but :397-399 applies any later version-detail response with setCompareBase/setBaseSystem. There is no sequence id, abort or cleanup for either request.
findings.expected: R-157: choosing a version 'diffs that version against the current system'; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: follow identifiers and 'context restoration ... alternate entry points' and ignore stale work after later decisions. The selected baseline must belong to the currently open project and latest selection.
reproduction_steps: Open project A > Compare and choose a saved version while the request is slow.
Open B before the version-detail response arrives.
Allow A's response to finish, then open Compare on B.
A's version is used as the baseline for B until a new selection replaces it.

findings.title: Returning to a project lets an obsolete regeneration replace its newly loaded version — the discard guard checks id but not editing lifecycle
findings.surface: Regenerate while switching away from and back to a project
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: start regenerating A v1, open B, then reopen A after another editor saved v2. When the original generation completes, the id comparison passes and it replaces v2 in the workspace with a revision based on v1; project metadata still holds v2, so saving that output does not trigger the overwrite warning. Users can silently reintroduce stale content despite the new discard guard. Saved history mitigates recovery, but the newly loaded collaborative state is not preserved.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:203 records only project_id and :209 compares only the final project_id. openProject at :336-339 can reload the same project at a newer version while a synthesis runs; :213-214 then installs the older closure's result/context if the final id equals the original, regardless of intervening switches/reloads.
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: 'stale work must respect later decisions'; request: teammates must not 'silently undo each other's work'. A revision started on A v1 must not replace a subsequently loaded A v2 merely because its project id is equal.
reproduction_steps: Start a regeneration on project A at v1.
Switch to B while it runs.
Have another editor save A v2, then reopen A in the first workspace.
Let the v1 generation finish: it is applied to the now-v2 workspace and can be saved without a conflict.

findings.title: Accepted PDF references can be invisible to the AI — only truncated extracted text is sent, never scanned pages
findings.surface: Attach reference > PDF > Synthesize
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: attach a scanned/image-only specification PDF. Upload succeeds and its chip is retained, but extract_text yields no content and no PDF page image or PDF bytes are sent to the AI. The reference in the prompt contains only its filename. Text-bearing content after page 40 or 20,000 characters is also silently omitted. The user believes the PDF grounded the synthesis but must manually convert/select its content to recover. This is source-predicted omission, not an executed judgment about model output.
findings.evidence: projects.py:306-307 extracts text from only the first 40 PDF pages and truncates to TEXT_CHARS=20000 (:23); upload stores that text at :347. load_references at :394-396 sends image bytes only when content_type starts with image/, not for PDFs. server.py:242 selects '(image attached below)' only for image_bytes, otherwise text or ''; :244 sends this as source material.
findings.expected: request: 'Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs, and code or text files' and 'The AI uses them as source material'; R-169: 'attached references ... in the shape that provider expects'; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: compare 'complete intended content and actual input selection'. Image-only PDF pages must reach the model or be rejected/explained instead of silently accepted as empty source.
reproduction_steps: Attach a PDF containing a scanned UI specification with no text layer.
Ask Synthesize to match the PDF's design.
Follow the reference path: its extracted text is empty and it is not added to image attachments.
The provider receives the filename but none of the scanned design.

findings.title: Some 503 responses fail without the promised retries — overload detection matches text formatting rather than the HTTP status
findings.surface: Gemini synthesis busy-response handling
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: a Gemini 503 exception with numeric status 503 but the quoted UNAVAILABLE/single-quoted error representation is not classified busy, so the first request fails immediately with generic provider text rather than receiving the two retries and busy explanation. Users facing transient overload lose an otherwise recoverable generation attempt and must retry manually. This is a conditional source trace for that exception shape, not an observed provider outage.
findings.evidence: classify_error at server.py:282 recognizes busy only through a few string fragments, including double-quoted '"code": 503', and never inspects an exception's status_code. :321 retries only if this classifier returns busy. A 503 exception rendered as "503 UNAVAILABLE. {'error': {'code': 503, 'message': 'The service is currently unavailable'}}" matches none of the fragments and falls through to generic 'error' at :284.
findings.expected: R-106: 'a 503 is retried twice before failing'; R-168: 'When Gemini returns 503 ... retries the same request twice ... reports a busy error'. Status-code identity is 503 regardless of capitalization, JSON versus Python-repr quotes or provider wording; use structured status/code information or cover that supported error shape.
reproduction_steps: Run a Gemini synthesis when the provider returns HTTP 503 with an UNAVAILABLE exception whose message is 'The service is currently unavailable' and whose error dict is rendered with single quotes.
The busy matcher sees neither its hardcoded words nor double-quoted code fragment.
The job fails after one attempt instead of three.

findings.title: A provider timeout produces an empty-cause error banner — synthesis error classification omits timeouts
findings.surface: Synthesis Failed banner; GET /api/generate/{job_id}
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: if generation's awaited provider call raises TimeoutError, run_job does end the job and preserves the previous project, but the user gets only 'AI provider error: ' and code='error'. The timeout cause is lost even though the key-test path knows how to explain it. Users cannot tell whether to fix their key, change input or retry. This is bounded error-recovery impairment; no timeout was induced.
findings.evidence: server.py:287-296 handles authentication/quota/model-unavailable substrings but has no timeout branch; an asyncio.TimeoutError has an empty str and returns 'AI provider error: '. run_job at :336-337 persists code='error' and that detail. test_key has its own explicit timeout explanation at :407-408, but generate does not.
findings.expected: R-105: failure 'shows a message in plain English naming that cause'; R-106 explicitly includes 'provider timeout' and machine-readable error_code; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: resolve failure with 'visible feedback and promised recovery'. A provider timeout must be identified as a timeout with usable retry guidance.
reproduction_steps: Start a generation whose provider request raises TimeoutError.
Poll the generation job.
The job is error with generic code and an empty-cause 'AI provider error: ' banner rather than a timeout message.

findings.title: Other open tabs keep using a removed or replaced key — key settings are read only when the workspace mounts
findings.surface: AI key Remove/Save across two open workspace tabs
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: two workspace tabs load key A. Removing or replacing it in tab 1 changes localStorage, but tab 2 retains and continues sending A with its old model until reloaded. A user rotating/removing a credential can unintentionally continue consuming that old key's quota or paid usage. This is limited to already mounted tabs; a newly opened or reloaded tab reads the correct saved setting.
findings.evidence: AiKeyModal.jsx:51-52 updates localStorage and :119 removes the saved item. Workspace.jsx:164 calls loadAiKey only as the initial useState initializer; its subsequent generate at :198 checks that in-memory value and :208 forwards it. No storage event subscription or per-generation reload exists in these paths.
findings.expected: R-165: 'after removal the Synthesize button returns to ... [the no-key prompt] and no job starts', and 'after replacement the next synthesis uses the new key and model'; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: 'Settings persist and affect the promised behaviour throughout the app.' Browser-local rotation/removal must take effect in already open tabs too, or the UI must explicitly limit the claim to the current tab.
reproduction_steps: Save key A, then open the workspace in a second tab.
In the first tab, Remove the key or replace it with B and save.
Without reloading, synthesize in the second tab.
Its request still carries A, and removal did not return it to the add-key prompt.

findings.title: Email/password invitees do not see invited projects on sign-in — automatic access is limited to Google-verified accounts
findings.surface: Projects → Shared with me; email sign-in
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an invited email/password user signs in successfully but Shared with me stays empty, including when the owner invited an already registered email account. They must obtain and follow the separate invite link to gain access, defeating the promised automatic discovery. Google sign-in is the only path that sets verification (:170).

findings.expected: R-077 and request: "The person sees the project under 'Shared with me' as soon as they sign in with that email." Both supported sign-in methods must reach this outcome while maintaining secure email identity.

As owner add that email as Viewer or Editor in Share.
Sign in as that teammate without opening the invite link.
Open Shared with me: the query excludes the pending membership.

findings.title: Reopened projects use another project's bias and omit saved notes — openSystem never restores these inputs
findings.surface: Projects → open; Project Context and Notes for next synthesis
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts opening project A saved with 'GAS with hard attribute ceiling' while the browser context is 'realistic large-scale FPS' leaves the FPS bias displayed and used in A's next regeneration. Notes that produced A are not restored to the notes control either. Saved context exists in Mongo but is ignored, so teammates and cross-device users must reconstruct it manually and can generate the wrong architecture.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:189 stores project_context and notes in result.context; :154 initializes projectContext from browser storage; :288-298 restores dials/prompt/references but never calls setProjectContext(c.project_context); :301 unconditionally setNotes(""). :187 injects the current global projectContext into every run.
findings.expected: R-062: reopening "restores those inputs and that system"; request: a project holds "description, dials, Project Context, modules and notes" and teammates regenerate together. Opening a cloud project must restore its own bias and notes rather than an unrelated browser default.
reproduction_steps: Generate and save A with one Project Context preset and designer notes.
Change the browser's context to a different preset while working on B.
Open A from Projects.
A's saved context and notes are not restored; Synthesize sends the other preset.

findings.title: Attaching or removing references on a saved project is lost on Save — persistence uses the last synthesis's stale reference list
findings.surface: Attach reference / remove chip → Save → reopen
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an Editor attaching a file after synthesis then saving sees the chip disappear on reopening. Conversely removing a reference and saving restores the removed chip on reopening, and a later regeneration sends that reference again. Uploading the object with a project id does not fix the issue because project reopening never discovers attached references from the file collection. Regenerating before Save is a costly, undisclosed workaround.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:156 maintains references separately; :189 copies them into result.context only when generation completes. :263-265 splitResult returns result.context unchanged; :270-274 saves that context. Files.jsx:43 and :61 update only the separate references state. openSystem at Workspace.jsx:298 restores context.references.
findings.expected: R-078: "each attached reference ... stays attached to the project for later regenerations"; request: "Each can be removed individually." Saving must persist the currently chosen reference list without requiring another paid synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Open a generated saved project.
Attach a new reference (or remove an existing reference chip).
Press Save without synthesizing again.
Reopen the project; the old reference list returns.

findings.title: Reloading or deep-linking a cloud project opens the default workspace — project identity is never retained in the URL
findings.surface: /projects/{id}; project open and page reload
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts opening /projects/<id> renders an unsaved default workspace, and reloading after opening a cloud project loses the selected project and inputs. Users must find it in Projects again; browser back/forward cannot return between project selections. Saved data remains recoverable through the list.
findings.evidence: App.js:27 routes every otherwise unmatched path to Workspace without extracting a project id. Workspace.jsx:168 only reads a ?project query; :171 immediately replaces even that URL with '/'. :305-311 opens project state without changing the URL.
findings.expected: R-113: "Opening /projects/{id} directly ... loads that project's saved system ... and a reload keeps the same project open"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "direct access, reload, back and return paths" must retain the referenced object.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing project from Projects.
Reload the page: the workspace initializes with no project.
Open /projects/<that id> in a fresh signed-in tab.
The catch-all renders the default workspace without loading the id.

findings.title: Accepted reference code and PDF content is silently omitted — extraction truncates at 20,000 characters and 40 pages
findings.surface: Attach reference → Synthesize
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts an accepted 30 KB .h whose class declaration lies after a long license/comment prefix loses that entire declaration before generation, and a PDF's page 41 is never considered. The chip still shows a successful attachment and the full file is stored, so developers pay for a synthesis that cannot follow the omitted specification without knowing to split/rewrite it. UTF-8 text and PDF extraction do reach Claude for content inside those silent bounds.
findings.evidence: projects.py:22 sets TEXT_CHARS=20000; :261 takes PDF pages[:40] then text[:TEXT_CHARS]; :265 truncates decoded code/text to 20000 characters. :299-304 stores the full original size and reports successful attachment without a truncation flag. server.py:230-232 sends only that extracted text.
findings.expected: R-104 and request: "AI uses them as source material", e.g. "extend this existing header"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content and actual input selection" and make skipped input visible. Within the stated 10 MB acceptance limit, required content must reach the model or limitations must be communicated before synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid UTF-8 header under 10 MB with the declared class after character 20,000 (or a spec with requirements on PDF page 41).
Ask to extend that class or implement that requirement and Synthesize.
The model prompt receives only the truncated prefix.
No attachment or generation UI reports that the required content was omitted.

findings.title: Abandoned synthesis keeps polling after navigation or sign-out — async polling has no lifecycle cancellation
findings.surface: Running synthesis → leave workspace/sign out
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts signing out or navigating to a public share view during generation leaves the old polling loop alive for up to five minutes, issuing requests and (after sign-out) refresh attempts. Returning and starting another run adds a separate loop; old completions still issue progress/result callbacks and success toasts. The UI cannot cancel the abandoned loop. Normal completion does stop its loop.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:43-50 loops with a new setTimeout and GET every two seconds until five minutes, done or error; there is no AbortSignal or mounted guard. Workspace's only effect at :164-174 returns no synthesis cleanup. AuthContext.jsx:31-33 can unmount Workspace on sign-out. The polling catch at Workspace.jsx:48-49 also ignores permanent 401/404.
findings.expected: R-118: polling "stops ... when ... user leaves the workspace"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner". Leaving a workspace must terminate its client polling and callbacks.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize on a slow job.
Sign out or navigate within the app to another routed surface before it finishes.
Return to the workspace and start another generation.
The first loop has no cleanup and keeps polling alongside the new one until its deadline/completion.

findings.title: Keyboard focus escapes modal dialogs into covered workspace actions — modal primitive supplies no focus management
findings.surface: Share, reset-link, migration and conflict modals
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts keyboard users opening Share remain focused on the background Share button and can Tab through covered Copy, Export, Save, description and project controls before reaching modal fields. They can invoke covered actions while a supposedly modal share/reset/conflict surface is open. Closing does not restore focus. Pointer users can use the modal normally; keyboard users must traverse unrelated controls and risk acting on background work.
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 only installs Escape; :11-12 renders aria-modal dialog/backdrop, but has no focus assignment, focus trap, background inertness or restore-focus logic. ShareModal.jsx:46 uses this primitive while Workspace's editing actions remain mounted; AccountMenu.jsx:19 uses it for admin reset.
findings.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus". Modal keyboard interaction must stay on the dialog rather than reaching covered workspace controls.
reproduction_steps: Focus the workspace Share button using the keyboard and press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly.
Focus is not moved into or contained by the Share dialog, so background controls remain in the tab order.
Close the modal with Escape; no focus restoration is performed.

findings.title: Files with non-Latin filenames cannot be downloaded — raw Unicode is placed into a latin-1 HTTP header
findings.surface: Files → Download; GET /api/files/{file_id}
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts uploading a valid file named '角色设计.txt' succeeds, but downloading it raises UnicodeEncodeError while constructing the response headers because those characters cannot be encoded as latin-1. A teammate/viewer receives a failed download instead of any bytes. An uploader could rename and re-upload outside the app, but recipients cannot fix the stored name themselves.
findings.evidence: projects.py:281 preserves arbitrary original filenames; :330 removes only double quotes and :331 interpolates the name directly into the Content-Disposition header of starlette Response. requirements.txt pins starlette 0.37.2; header values use HTTP latin-1 encoding rather than Unicode filename* encoding. Files.jsx:19 needs that GET to succeed before creating a blob download.
findings.expected: R-080/R-081: downloading returns "original name and identical bytes"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: preserve "encoding ... filename". A valid Unicode filename must not prevent delivery; use an encoded filename* with a safe fallback.
reproduction_steps: Upload a small project file named 角色设计.txt.
Open Files as a member and press Download.
The download endpoint attempts to place that raw name in its response header and fails before delivering the file.

findings.title: Compare hides parameter/module/note edits and misstates old module selection — it discards those input changes and snapshots edited state
findings.surface: Compare → Input changes and Parameters & Modules
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a regeneration changing Max Health, toggling StaminaDrain and adding notes opens Compare with no corresponding Input changes chips. Its Parameters & Modules view also uses the already-toggled old module state, so a module removal can show no before/after module difference. Code/text line diff still works, but users cannot reliably audit which requested edits produced it.
findings.evidence: CompareView.jsx:34 passes params:{} and notes:"" to computeChanges and :35 removes every module change. Workspace.jsx:248-254 mutates result.modules before regeneration; :188 sets that already-edited result as previousResult. computeChanges (changes.js:27-40) only detects params/notes when supplied and needs original module state.
findings.expected: R-094: Compare "lists which inputs changed" across "parameters and modules"; request: "see the effect of dial or prompt changes"; R-086 includes parameter values, module toggles/additions and notes. Compare's previous side and changed-input list must reflect the actual previous synthesis, not edited chips.
reproduction_steps: Generate a system with a parameter and an enabled module.
Change that parameter, toggle the module off, add notes and Synthesize.
Inspect Compare's Input changes: those edits are omitted.
Switch to Parameters & Modules: the previous module is already off, hiding the actual toggle.

findings.title: Cloud projects lose their before/after comparison on reopening — only the current synthesis is persisted
findings.surface: Saved cloud project → Compare
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts a developer synthesizing twice, comparing and saving a cloud project loses the previous side after reload/reopen. Another Editor opening that saved project cannot inspect the changes at all. They must pay for another regeneration just to create a new pair, and the original comparison cannot be reconstructed through the app because the previous output was discarded.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:152 previousResult is only React state; :188 assigns it after an in-session run. splitResult :263-265 exports/saves result only, with no previousResult. openSystem :300 explicitly clears previousResult. backend/projects.py:127-132 stores only current system/context; :169-172 replaces them on save. CompareView.jsx:44-49 then shows 'Synthesize twice'.
findings.expected: R-095's independently checkable outcome is retrieval of previous/current sections for a cloud project; request: "Stack Systems and Compare keep working with cloud projects" and Phase 2 adds "any earlier version, not just the last one." Phase 1 should retain the immediate before/after comparison across save and reopen, without requiring full Phase 2 history or a particular API route.
reproduction_steps: Generate, tune and regenerate a system, then inspect Compare.
Save the project and reopen it (or open it on another device).
Open Compare: only the empty 'Synthesize twice' message is available.
No saved previous synthesis or changed-input record can be loaded.

findings.title: Retrying browser migration duplicates saved systems — every import mints a fresh project with no legacy identity
findings.surface: First-sign-in browser migration → Import them
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts clicking Import them twice while migration is in progress or retrying its request duplicates each legacy system under fresh ids. The modal remains actionable throughout and the backend has no idempotency key. The user's cloud library becomes cluttered with duplicate projects; manual deletion is the safe recovery.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:330-334 posts every migration item to /projects/import and the Import them button at :752 has no busy guard. projects.py:152 calls create each time; :128 mints a new project_id and :133 inserts without a legacy-source identity check. server.py:42-49 has no owner/legacy-id uniqueness index.
findings.expected: R-085: posting the same browser library twice "creates no duplicate project"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record/operation/effect identity ... retries ... concurrent creation." A given browser-saved system imported by one migration intent must create one cloud copy, while distinct legacy systems remain distinct.
reproduction_steps: Have multiple systems in the old browser library and sign in for the first time.
Click Import them twice before the first network loop finishes (or retry the same import payload).
Both loops POST the same entries.
Mine contains separately identified duplicates of each imported system.

findings.title: Failed browser migrations cannot be retried in the app — failures are swallowed and the one-time prompt is marked complete
findings.surface: Browser migration partial-failure path
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a transient network/storage failure during first migration leaves some or all systems unimported, then permanently suppresses the offer and labels the operation with a success toast. The raw legacy data remains in localStorage, but the new cloud-only library has no control to reopen or retry that browser library, so the user cannot recover through the intended UI without developer/storage intervention.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:334 swallows every failed per-item import; :336 emits a success toast even for zero imported; :339 writes the migration-completed key regardless of failures and :340 closes the modal. Initialization at :166-167 offers migration only if that key is absent. Browser data is not removed, but no retry UI exists.
findings.expected: R-084: "Import creates one project per browser system"; request: "Import them copies them into the account"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches ... visible rejected/skipped input". Partial failures must be explained and retryable rather than marking unfinished migration complete.
reproduction_steps: Start first-sign-in Import them with legacy systems present.
Have one or more POST /projects/import requests fail (e.g. a transient network interruption).
After the loop the modal closes and reports Imported N of M.
Reload: the completion marker prevents another migration offer despite the missing projects.

findings.title: Double-clicking Save project creates duplicate cloud projects — initial save has no pending guard or operation identity
findings.surface: Save project; POST /api/projects
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer double-clicking Save project on an unsaved synthesis gets two distinct cloud projects. The UI provides no pending state and both calls show success. Manual deletion is a safe but unnecessary cleanup; this is separate from migration duplication because normal saves use a different entry point and have no migration source id.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:418 Save is disabled only when !result or readOnly, not while saving. :272-274 uses captured project state; before the first POST resolves, a second call still sees project null and POSTs again. projects.py:128/133 always mints and inserts another project, with no create operation identity.
findings.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create ... per intent"; request: "Save ... work as they do today, but in the cloud." Repeated clicks during a single initial Save should create one project.
reproduction_steps: Generate an unsaved system.
Click Save project twice before the first request returns.
Both captured calls choose POST /projects.
Projects → Mine contains two copies of the same initial save.

findings.title: Malformed imported project JSON crashes the workspace after being saved — importer validates only system_name
findings.surface: Projects → Import; POST /api/projects/import
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts importing valid JSON with a system_name but tunable_parameters set to a string (or non-array modules) stores the record and then causes an uncaught frontend TypeError when ProjectsPanel opens it. The workspace becomes unusable rather than explaining the invalid file. Reload resets the open project, allowing the user to delete the broken row; ordinary valid exports do round-trip system/context correctly.
findings.evidence: projects.py:125 checks only truthy system_name; :147 accepts the whole imported dict as a system and :151-152 stores it without SystemOutput validation. Workspace.jsx:299 renders it, :362 calls tunable_parameters.forEach and :659 calls modules.map. No error boundary is present in App.js:32-40.
findings.expected: Checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "malformed/partial input ... visible rejected/skipped input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "fields, types" must match at both ends; R-082/R-083 promise usable project import. Malformed project JSON must be refused without storing a broken project or crashing the workspace.
reproduction_steps: Use Import project with a JSON object containing system_name 'Broken' and tunable_parameters 'bad'.
The server accepts it because system_name is truthy.
The import UI immediately opens it.
Workspace's forEach/map assumptions throw instead of showing an import-validation message.

findings.title: Incomplete or unhonored generations are reported as successful — output validation checks types but not required content or edit coverage
findings.surface: Claude response → completed synthesis and Applied in this synthesis
findings.observed: AI and model features: source proves that if Claude returns a JSON object with all required keys but empty code, empty graph/setup lists, no applied_changes, or a tunable value different from an explicit override, the backend records done and the UI announces success. A user requesting Max Health=250 can receive and save a 100-valued output, with no row explaining that edit; empty output is also accepted. This is a conditional source trace of an accepted bad provider reply, not an observed model failure. Users must manually audit/retry paid generations instead of trusting the promised feedback.
findings.evidence: server.py:128 makes setup why optional with default ''; :150 defaults applied_changes to []; :143-148 accepts empty code strings and empty graph/setup lists. :303 performs only SystemOutput(**data), then :308 marks done. There is no comparison against req.change_requests, req.parameter_overrides or required output completeness. ChangePanels.jsx:36-38 hides the panel entirely when changes are absent.
findings.expected: R-087: "one applied entry per queued change"; R-089: why notes explain setup decisions; R-097: non-empty complete code/graph/setup; R-102: requested values are used. Checklist, AI and model features: "parsing, semantic validation ... empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." A structurally valid but incomplete/unapplied reply must not be confirmed as completed synthesis.
reproduction_steps: Queue a parameter change and a designer note, then Synthesize.
Consider a provider reply with the expected field types but applied_changes omitted and tunable value unchanged (or empty code/graph lists).
SystemOutput validation accepts it and marks the job done.
The UI shows success and hides the missing change report rather than rejecting/reconciling the incomplete result.

findings.title: One reset link can change the password twice concurrently — token consumption happens after an unguarded password write
findings.surface: POST /api/auth/reset-password; reset link redemption
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two concurrent requests with the same reset link and different new passwords can both observe used=False and both report success, with the second password winning. The first user is then unable to sign in with the password the screen confirmed. A person retaining the same reset URL can race a legitimate redemption; another admin reset link is needed to recover safely.
findings.evidence: auth.py:229 reads a reset record; :230 checks used; :232 changes the password; only afterward :233 sets used=True using a token-only filter. There is no atomic used=False claim or transaction before the password write. ResetPassword in AuthPages.jsx:42-58 has no busy guard against overlapping submissions.
findings.expected: R-059: the reset token is "single-use" and "a second use ... is refused"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must preserve effect identity under concurrent requests. Only one password change may succeed for a given token.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a fresh on-screen reset link.
Submit that token concurrently from two clients with different valid new passwords, before either marks it used.
Both requests can pass the unused check and update the password.
Only the last password works despite both submissions reporting success.

findings.title: Google-first users cannot add email/password sign-in themselves — registration rejects their email and no password-linking flow exists
findings.surface: Google-first account → email registration/sign-in
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Google-first user trying Create account with the same email is refused, and Sign in with email always fails because no password exists. They can continue using Google, but cannot add the promised second method without owner-assisted password reset, which is not an ordinary self-service linking flow.
findings.evidence: auth.py:174-178 creates Google-first users without password_hash. :128-129 rejects every registration for an existing email; :148 rejects email sign-in when password_hash is missing. No set-password/account-link action exists in AccountMenu.jsx:58-65; only an admin can issue a reset link (:214-224).
findings.expected: R-055: "Signing in with Google ... and later registering with email/password ... reaches one account"; request: "Two ways to sign in ... If both use the same email address, they reach the same account." Provide a secure authenticated way to add the password method to the existing account, without creating a duplicate.
reproduction_steps: Sign in for the first time using Google and save a project.
Sign out and choose Create account with the same email and a password.
Registration says the account already exists.
Try email Sign in: the Google-first record has no password, and there is no account control to set one.

findings.title: Older projects and files silently disappear from their lists — fixed 500-record caps have no pagination or truncation notice
findings.surface: Projects lists and Files tab at more than 500 records
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that once a user has 501 live owned projects (including repeated imports) their oldest project disappears from Mine and the count reads 500, with no way to load the remaining page. Likewise a project's 501st-oldest file is omitted from Files. Records are still stored and retrievable if an id was retained, but ordinary users cannot discover/download older work through the UI on a new device.
findings.evidence: projects.py:113/:117 use to_list(500) with no skip/cursor/total; :322 also caps file listing at 500. ProjectsPanel.jsx:71 labels lists[id].length as the count and :86 renders only those rows, with no paging/Load more action. ProjectFiles similarly renders the returned files only (:119).
findings.expected: Request: cloud Projects "saved safely and available on any device" and Files keeps project artifacts; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation" and "counts ... match the rows they summarize." All stored accessible projects/files must remain discoverable as the library grows.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate or import 501 distinct projects in one account.
Open Projects → Mine; only the newest 500 appear with count 500.
Look for the oldest project or a next-page control: neither is available.
The same cutoff applies after uploading more than 500 project files.

findings.title: Image-only PDFs are accepted but invisible to Claude — PDF processing extracts text only and sends no visual pages
findings.surface: PDF reference attachment → Synthesize
findings.observed: AI and model features: source predicts a scanned spec or PDF containing a UI screenshot but no text layer uploads successfully yet supplies an empty body to Claude. No PDF bytes or rendered page images reach the model and no empty-extraction warning appears. The designer's request to match that PDF cannot be grounded in its actual content; converting it manually to an image is a safe workaround once the limitation is discovered.
findings.evidence: projects.py:261 uses only PdfReader page.extract_text() for PDF references. upload_file :294-295 calls it for any non-image reference; load_references :347-349 attaches image_bytes only when content_type starts image/. server.py:230 sends extracted PDF text, while :285 includes only image_bytes as visual content.
findings.expected: Request: "Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs" and "The AI uses them as source material"; R-104; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace "complete intended content and actual input selection". A valid PDF whose content is graphical must reach the model visually or be explicitly rejected/warned, not silently treated as empty source.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid image-only PDF under 10 MB containing the desired UI/spec.
Ask Synthesize to follow it.
extract_text returns empty text and no image_bytes are generated for application/pdf.
The model request contains the filename but none of the PDF's visible source content.

findings.title: Notes typed while a synthesis is running disappear on completion — the old request unconditionally clears the live draft
findings.surface: Notes for next synthesis during a running generation
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer entering new notes for the next pass while Claude is generating loses those notes when the old request completes. They were not in that request's body, are not in result.context, and are erased from the visible field with no warning. Rewriting the short draft is the only recovery; controls suggest editing remains allowed during generation.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits the long-running job; :189 snapshots the notes submitted at start; :190 unconditionally clears the live notes state on completion. The notes textarea at :702-710 is inside a fieldset disabled only by readOnly (:608), not loading, so users can keep editing notes while the job runs.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: input and operation state must remain coherent. R-086/request: notes before the next Synthesize must be injected rather than silently discarded.
reproduction_steps: Start a synthesis or regeneration.
While it is running, type a new note such as 'use a Gameplay Tag for stun' in Notes for next synthesis.
Wait for the current job to complete.
The new note disappears although it was never sent to that job or saved in its context.

findings.title: Reloading strands the paid synthesis result — the only job handle exists inside the old polling call
findings.surface: Running background synthesis → browser reload
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts reloading during a generation loses the job id and returns to an idle workspace even though the server keeps generating and spending the owner's credits. The completed result remains in Mongo but is unreachable through any workspace/library action; only someone who retained the API id can retrieve it. The ordinary UI recovery is to pay for another synthesis. Normal uninterrupted polling delivers the result.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:36-38 keeps job_id only in a local async variable; no component/localStorage/project field stores it and mount at :164-174 loads only templates/migration/query project. server.py:315-318 persists jobs but only :325-330 GET-by-id retrieves them; there is no current/recent job lookup or result recovery consumer.
findings.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "interruption ... revisit ... resume ... retrieves the completed session" where supported; users rely on: "A paid background synthesis can be retrieved after an ordinary page reload rather than requiring a second paid run." R-099/R-100 describe server background generation and delivery of its finished system.
reproduction_steps: Press Synthesize and wait until the background job has started.
Reload the browser before it finishes.
The new workspace starts idle with no resume/recent-job control.
Allow the original job to finish: it is not shown or recoverable in Projects unless the original page had saved its result.

findings.title: Oversized uploads can exhaust worker memory before rejection — file limits are checked only after an unbounded read
findings.surface: POST /api/files oversized uploads
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts a signed-in user's oversized 1 GB upload is fully read into a bytes object before its eventual 413, and concurrent such uploads multiply the allocation. The documented 25 MB ceiling therefore does not bound worker memory, risking interruptions to other users' saves/generations under a reachable large-upload workload. No runtime memory/latency measurement was made; exact failure depends on deployment memory.
findings.evidence: projects.py:284 executes data = await file.read() without a size bound, then :285-287 applies 10/25 MB limits using len(data). The multipart UploadFile may be disk-spooled, but this call materializes the entire uploaded body in application memory before rejection.
findings.expected: Request: "10 MB per reference file and 25 MB per project file"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "buffering ... bounds and backpressure" must prevent material resource growth for reachable input. Oversized uploads must be rejected without unbounded application-memory buffering.
reproduction_steps: As a member with Editor access, upload a project file much larger than 25 MB.
The endpoint reads the full file into memory first.
Only after that allocation does it return the size-limit error.
Concurrent oversized uploads repeat that full allocation per request.

findings.title: Admin reset-link creation stops working after access-token expiry — refresh interceptor skips protected auth routes
findings.surface: Account menu → Password reset link → Create
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an email-signed-in admin waiting over 15 minutes then choosing Password reset link receives 'Not authenticated' on Create, repeatedly, despite the still-valid refresh session. Other project API calls refresh automatically, but this action never does. Reloading or forcing an unrelated project request restores it; this is bounded but confusing account-management failure.
findings.evidence: api.js:11 excludes every URL beginning /auth/ from refresh/retry. AccountMenu.jsx:14 posts /auth/admin/reset-link, whose backend Depends(admin_user) calls current_user and returns 401 after the 15-minute access expiry (auth.py:16,86-96). The refresh cookie remains valid seven days (:17,42).

An active admin with a valid refresh session must not need unrelated navigation or reload for this protected account action.

Wait beyond the 15-minute access-token lifetime without making a refreshing API call.
Open Account menu → Password reset link and press Create for a valid user.
