findings.title: Viewer project regeneration is restricted only in the UI — generation requests have no enforced project identity or Editor check
findings.surface: POST /api/generate project regeneration
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Viewer sending a project regeneration directly can start a paid Claude job and obtain its revised output because project identity is ignored, whereas the UI says regeneration requires Editor access. Saving back to the shared project is correctly refused, so this is a bounded generation-role violation rather than unauthorized durable project mutation. The endpoint must distinguish an allowed new personal synthesis from a regeneration of an existing role-restricted project.
findings.evidence: server.py:77 configures extra='ignore'; GenerateRequest :79-95 has no project_id and generate_system :312 requires only current_user, not load_project(..., 'editor'). Workspace.jsx:213-221 sends a previous system without project identity; only the frontend readOnly flag at :161 and fieldsets prevent Viewer synthesis. In contrast projects.py:163 and :279-280 do check editor access for saves/uploads.
findings.expected: R-073: "a generate request attributed to that project [from a Viewer is] refused ... while ... Editor ... succeed"; request: "Viewer: can open, copy, export and download only"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: reject "client-only checks without server enforcement." Project regeneration must enforce the current project's role server-side.
reproduction_steps: Open a project shared as Viewer and note that Synthesize is disabled.
Using an authorized API client, submit its regeneration request with that project's identity and previous output.
GenerateRequest ignores the project identity and starts a job for the Viewer.
The same request is never checked against the member's current Viewer role.

findings.title: Accepted long passwords ignore their suffix, so an old password can survive reset — bcrypt's 72-byte limit conflicts with the 128-character input contract
findings.surface: Email registration, sign-in and password reset with long/Unicode passwords
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two accepted passwords sharing the first 72 UTF-8 bytes but differing later authenticate as the same password. A user resetting an 80-character passphrase by changing its tail can still sign in with the old password, and Unicode passwords reach this byte boundary with fewer than 72 characters. The remaining prefix still supplies entropy, so the evidence supports a bounded password-identity failure rather than a general bypass. Users are not told to change the earlier prefix to recover.
findings.evidence: auth.py:102/:113 accepts passwords up to 128 characters, :24 hashes password.encode() directly and :28 verifies the same way. backend/requirements.txt:9 pins bcrypt==4.1.3, whose bcrypt input semantics use only the first 72 bytes. There is no byte-length validator or full-length prehash.
findings.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "password hashing" and valid/wrong-password handling must preserve the supported password's identity; users rely on: "All characters of an accepted password determine whether it authenticates." For a reset, changing a supported password must invalidate the old distinct password, not ignore its suffix.
reproduction_steps: Register using a valid password longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes but within the 128-character limit.
Through a fresh reset link choose a different password with the same first 72 bytes and a changed suffix.
Sign out and try the old password.
bcrypt 4.1.3 ignores the differing suffix and accepts the old password too.

findings.title: Retrying a lost synthesis response spends credits twice — generation creation has no stable operation identity
findings.surface: Synthesize → ambiguous initial network failure → retry
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that if the server creates a job but its initial POST response is lost, the UI immediately reports failure and allows Retry/Synthesize. Retrying creates a second independent Claude call while the first continues spending credits; the first result is unreachable through the UI. Any signed-in developer on an unreliable connection can unintentionally charge the owner twice for one requested synthesis. The issue is retry identity, distinct from duplicate cloud Save records.
findings.evidence: Workspace.jsx:38-40 treats a failed POST response as a failed generation without reconciling a possible job already started. server.py:314-319 creates a fresh random job id and task on every POST, with no caller-supplied operation key/unique intent lookup. The client retains no pending operation handle before the POST response.
findings.expected: Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "retries ... preserve the operation's identity" and "a send timing out after delivery must reconcile before retrying"; request: "Every AI generation ... is paid from the app owner's ... balance." One synthesis intent must not incur two generations solely because its accepted response was lost.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize.
Have the initial POST response fail after the backend has inserted the job and started its task.
After the visible Generation failed message, press Synthesize again.
The backend starts a second job rather than returning/recovering the first operation.

findings.title: Reopened systems regenerate from an unrelated description — the library saves output but not its generation context
findings.surface: Save → My Library → Synthesize System
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a developer who saves an inventory system, reloads the page, opens it and adjusts a parameter sends the initial melee-combat prompt (:164), ActorComponent and default architecture settings to the model. The saved inventory parameters are mixed into that combat request. Similarly, opening a different saved system retains the preceding system's prompt/settings. The output can be viewed correctly, but continuing customization of saved work requires manually reconstructing the description and settings; they are not recoverable from the saved record. The wrong request is source-proven; the model's resulting content is not observed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:241 stores only `{ ...result, saved_at: ... }`; :244-247 loadFromLibrary only calls setResult(item) and setTab("graph"); :200-210 generates from current prompt, bpClass, dials, replicated and extra rather than the saved system. backend/server.py:61-74 SystemOutput has no original prompt or generation settings.
findings.expected: request: "Save/manage generated systems in a personal library" selected through "All of the above", and "outputs were tunable via sliders ... alterations/customizations"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "revisit reaches valid work for the same operation." Loading a saved system for further tuning must restore that system's original generation context rather than silently use another system's prompt.
reproduction_steps: Choose Grid Inventory, change its architecture dials or NET setting, synthesize, and Save.
Reload the page.
Open the saved inventory entry in My Library.
Adjust one System Parameter and press Synthesize System.
The submitted prompt is the default melee-combat prompt and the saved generation settings have not been restored.

findings.title: C++ code displays corrupted markup instead of clean highlighted code — regex passes rewrite their own HTML tags
findings.surface: C++ Snippets code viewers
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: any generated C++ containing a comment or string triggers overlapping substitutions. For example, the quotes in the tok-com class attribute are themselves replaced with a tok-str span, and subsequent keyword replacement rewrites the literal class attribute names. Thus the highlighter returns malformed nested markup which the browser must repair, exposing markup fragments and corrupting the code's visual rendering. Developers cannot reliably read the C++ in the viewer, although Copy/download still use the original code and provide a recovery path. This conclusion comes from tracing the string transformations, not a browser observation.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/highlight.js:20 wraps comments in `<span class="tok-com">`; :22 applies its string regex to the entire resulting HTML, including the new class attribute; :27-28 applies CPP_KEYWORDS, which contains "class" (:3), to the whole HTML again. frontend/src/App.js:102,127 inserts that string with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
findings.expected: request: "All of the above" includes readable C++ snippets; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content ... with delivered output." Highlighting must preserve the exact visible code and only decorate tokens, not tokenize the HTML it just generated.
reproduction_steps: Synthesize a system whose C++ contains a normal // comment and a quoted include filename.
Open C++ Snippets.
The highlighter wraps the comment, then matches quotes and the word class inside its generated tags, producing malformed viewer HTML.

findings.title: Excluding a custom module sends contradictory instructions — the module remains in both include and remove lists
findings.surface: Modules → add module → generated module chip → Synthesize System; POST /api/generate
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: add StaminaDrain, synthesize an output containing it, toggle its generated chip off, and synthesize again. StaminaDrain is still in extra and is also in removed, so the backend explicitly instructs the model both to include and exclude the same logical module. The requested exclusion is not represented as a single authoritative decision, making the advertised add/subtract flow unreliable and requiring the user to discover and remove the separate extra chip as well. The contradictory request is source-proven; which instruction the model follows is not observed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:235 adds the name to extra; :225-230 toggles only result.modules[].included, never extra; :198 builds removed from false modules and :208-209 sends extra_modules: extra and removed_modules: removed. backend/server.py:140-141 labels the same lists "User-added modules to INCLUDE" and "User-removed modules to mark excluded"; :100 asks for included:true and included:false respectively.
findings.expected: request: "some type of add/subtract options to integrate/expand upon"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "repeated toggles preserve the chosen state." A module toggled off must be unambiguously excluded on the next synthesis, not simultaneously demanded as included.
reproduction_steps: Add StaminaDrain in Modules and synthesize.
Toggle the generated StaminaDrain chip from included to excluded.
Leave the separate added-module chip in place and press Synthesize System.
The request includes StaminaDrain in both extra_modules and removed_modules.

findings.title: A malformed model parameter can blank the workspace — nested output records are accepted without the types the UI requires
findings.surface: POST /api/generate result → System Parameters
findings.observed: AI and model features: a provider result containing an otherwise valid SystemOutput with a parameter such as {key:'max_health', label:{text:'Max Health'}, value:100} passes the backend's List[dict] validation. The result is announced as generated and set into React state; rendering the object as Slider's label throws React's invalid-child error, unmounting the workspace rather than producing the intended retryable generation failure. The same weakness affects module and setup text fields. This is a conditional source-backed failure for malformed provider JSON, not a claim that Claude emitted it during this review. Reload can recover previously saved systems, but the just-generated work is lost.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:65 declares tunable_parameters: List[dict], :66 modules: List[dict], :70 setup_guide: List[dict]; :183 validates SystemOutput and :188 sends it as result. frontend/src/App.js:502 passes p.label directly to Slider; :65 renders {label}, and :66 renders {value}. frontend/src/index.js:17-23 mounts App without an error boundary.
findings.expected: checklist, AI and model features: "Follow parsing, semantic validation ... against the ... field/format ... contract" and "Trace empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." The backend should enforce the nested shapes required by its consumers and show a recoverable generation error for invalid output rather than accept a result that crashes the app.
reproduction_steps: Synthesize a system.
Consider the reachable provider-response condition that one tunable parameter's label is an object rather than a string while all top-level fields are present.
The backend accepts this dictionary and emits a result event.
The System Parameters render attempts to place the object in a span and the app has no error boundary.

findings.title: Narrow-screen users cannot read generated output — fixed sidebars consume more than the entire viewport
findings.surface: Workspace on narrow screens; all center output tabs
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: at 375px the two nonshrinking sidebars require 320+340=660px before any output space is allocated. The main has min-width:0 and consequently collapses to zero width; its Event Graph clips all nodes and its other output views have no usable reading width. Hiding tab text below lg does not free the sidebar allocation. Developers using narrow screens can generate but cannot use the central viewers normally; an export/another device may recover the text, so this is graded as a bounded presentation/interaction impairment. This is a source-based layout prediction, not a browser measurement.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:303 uses a single horizontal flex row; :306 fixes the left aside to w-[320px] shrink-0; :476 fixes the right aside to w-[340px] shrink-0, with no responsive variants; :382 main is flex-1 min-w-0. NodeGraph.jsx:67 clips overflow in its w-full canvas. The only responsive changes to tabs (:404) and chips (:293) hide labels, not the panels.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Check containment ... and reachable controls under supported viewports" and "primary content ... without ... clipping." Users rely on: "the web app lets them read generated output on a narrow screen, not just submit the description." At 375px the panels should reflow/collapse or provide a usable output pane.
reproduction_steps: Open the app with a 375px-wide viewport.
Synthesize a system.
Try Event Graph, C++ Snippets and Setup Guide.
Both fixed-width sidebars remain in the row, leaving the center output pane no allocated width.

findings.title: Save reports success and can crash when storage is full — persistence errors are uncaught and occur after confirmation
findings.surface: Save / My Library; useLibrary persistence effect
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: when the saved collection exceeds the browser's storage quota (or storage writes are denied), Save first reports success and then the effect throws. Persistence has not happened and the unhandled effect error can unmount the workspace; reloading restores only the previous collection, losing the allegedly saved generation. No limit, eviction, write error handling or in-memory recovery is implemented. This is a conditional source prediction, not a storage-quota test. It affects developers accumulating systems or running under storage restrictions; they can recover older saves on reload, but not trust the new-save confirmation.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:55 catches read/parse failures but :57 calls localStorage.setItem(LS_KEY, JSON.stringify(items)) in an effect with no try/catch. :241 updates React state and :242 immediately reports "Saved to library", before that effect persists the new collection. frontend/src/index.js:17-23 has no error boundary.
findings.expected: request: "Save/manage generated systems in a personal library" selected through "All of the above"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "A failed save ... [must not be] presented as confirmed"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "caches/queues have effective bounds or eviction." A full or unavailable local store must show a recoverable save failure and preserve the current generated system.
reproduction_steps: Use My Library until a further full-collection write would exceed the browser's local-storage quota, or use a browser context denying storage writes.
Synthesize another system and press Save.
The app reports Saved to library before attempting the uncaught write.
Reload: the newly confirmed save is not in the durable library.

findings.title: Saving in a second tab deletes the first tab's saved work — each tab overwrites storage from a stale library snapshot
findings.surface: My Library / Save in two browser tabs
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: open two tabs with the same initial library. Tab A saves system A, then tab B saves distinct system B. B merges against its stale React array and overwrites localStorage without A. Reloading either tab now permanently loses A from My Library, despite A having received a successful save confirmation. There is no server copy or import path to restore it. The overwritten record may still be visible in tab A until it is closed/reloaded, allowing a temporary manual re-save, but ordinary multiple-tab use silently loses valid saved work.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:54-55 reads the library only in the useState initializer; :57 overwrites the entire stored array on each local change; :241 merges a save only into that tab's lib snapshot. No storage listener or later storage read exists in App.js to reconcile another tab's updates.
findings.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Walk plausible interleavings ... Check ... lost/overwritten valid work ... using actors the app can actually run concurrently." Users rely on: "saving a different system in a second browser tab does not delete previously saved systems." Independently generated systems have distinct backend UUIDs (backend/server.py:181) and must coexist.
reproduction_steps: Open the app in two tabs before saving either new system.
In tab A synthesize and Save system A.
In tab B synthesize and Save a different system B.
Reload tab A: system A is gone from My Library.

findings.title: Long descriptions fail without telling developers what to fix — the UI omits the API limit and discards field-validation errors
findings.surface: AI Synthesizer prompt → Synthesize System; 422 error rendering
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: entering a detailed 2001-character system description is allowed by the UI, but FastAPI rejects it with an array-valued validation detail. streamGenerate discards the field and rule and displays only Request failed (422). No character limit/count is exposed, so the developer cannot tell whether the description, sliders or another setting caused the refusal and must guess what to edit. Shortening the prompt can recover the main task; the defect is opaque, mismatched validation, not an API failure to enforce its limit.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:32 enforces prompt max_length=2000. frontend/src/App.js:313-320 renders a textarea with no maxLength or length message; :191 checks only a lower bound; :30-31 discards non-string j.detail and substitutes `Request failed (${res.status})`. FastAPI's supplied HTTPValidationError schema defines detail as an array of loc/msg/type records (openapi.json, components.schemas.HTTPValidationError).
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Error messages identify the violated rule beside its field"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Compare request/response contracts at both ends ... error keys." A developer whose description exceeds the API's 2000-character contract should see the prompt limit and know how to correct it, rather than a generic status code.
reproduction_steps: Enter a system description of 2001 characters in AI Synthesizer.
Press Synthesize System.
Observe the source-predicted Synthesis Failed message Request failed (422), without the prompt's 2000-character limit.

findings.title: Touch and keyboard users cannot reach offscreen graph nodes — panning is mouse-only and zoom cannot fit the graph
findings.surface: Event Graph pan/drag on touch or keyboard input
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: on a 1024px-wide touch-only viewport, at most 1024-660=364px remains for the graph. A valid rightmost node at x=1200 extends to (1200+190)*0.4=556px even at minimum zoom. The canvas is overflow-hidden, has no scroll/pan alternative, and responds only to mouse dragging; tapping its zoom buttons cannot expose that final node. Keyboard-only users face the same lack of a pan action. The graph cannot be fully inspected under these supported browser input conditions, although textual outputs remain alternatives. This is a source-based reachability calculation, not a touch-device test.
findings.evidence: NodeGraph.jsx:69-72 installs only onMouseDown/onMouseMove/onMouseUp/onMouseLeave; :114 node dragging also uses onMouseDown. There are no touch/pointer/keyboard pan handlers. :67 clips overflow and :77 limits minimum zoom to 0.4. App.js:306,476 reserves 660px for sidebars. backend/server.py:97 permits nodes at x=1200; NodeGraph.jsx:55 fixes nodeWidth=190.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Follow shared event handling for keyboard, pointer, touch or assistive use"; request: "All of the above" includes node graphs visualized. Users must be able to reach all nodes on a touch device or with keyboard navigation, not only with a mouse.
reproduction_steps: Use a touch-only 1024px-wide browser (or keyboard-only navigation).
Generate a graph with a node at x=1200, within the backend prompt's specified layout range.
Use the − button down to its minimum zoom.
Attempt to pan to the last node: mouse-only handlers provide no touch or keyboard action, and the rightmost area remains clipped.

findings.title: Screen-reader users cannot identify tuning controls or compact tabs — visible labels are not accessible control names
findings.surface: Architecture Dials, System Parameters, and compact output-tab buttons
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: all architecture and generated-parameter range inputs lack accessible names because their text spans are not associated with them. A screen-reader user hears values but cannot reliably identify the setting being customized. Below the lg breakpoint, tab text is removed from the accessibility tree by display:none as well, leaving no textual tab names. The controls are keyboard-focusable, but operation by value/position guesswork is not equivalent to named controls. This is source-backed missing labeling, not an assistive-technology runtime observation; description-based generation remains an alternative, so the supported impact is bounded customization/navigation impairment.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:65 renders slider labels as an unrelated span, while :68-74 supplies the input no id, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. :398-405 gives tab buttons only an icon and a `hidden lg:inline` text span; the buttons have no aria-label or title when that span is display:none. These are the actual controls used at :483-486 and :499-509.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "Follow shared event handling for ... assistive use" and "reachable controls". Users rely on: "assistive technology identifies which architecture or system parameter a slider changes and which output tab a button opens." Visible text must programmatically label its control, with tab names retained when visually hidden.
reproduction_steps: Navigate the workspace using a screen reader.
Focus the Complexity, Modularity and generated System Parameter range controls.
Their visible text has no programmatic association with the focused input.
At a viewport below lg, focus each output-tab button: its textual name is hidden and there is no alternate label.

findings_minor.title: Owners see their team projects twice with duplicate counts — Mine query does not exclude team assignments

Move that project into the team.
Check Mine and Team: both contain it.

findings_minor.title: Reset users cannot confirm their new password — form has only one password input
findings_minor.surface: Reset password form
findings_minor.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a typo meeting the eight-character minimum becomes the account password immediately. Users can recover with another emailed reset, but the requested mismatch safeguard is absent.

findings_minor.title: Team access roster omits member names and owner email — API and modal expose only invitee emails in a mixed pending/joined list
findings_minor.surface: Projects > Team > Manage/Members
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: team owners/members can inspect email and role for invitees but cannot see their names or the owner's email, and pending invitations are interleaved with actual members. findings_minor.title: Undoing a fix can leave its old save note attached to another version — pre-filled saveNote is not cleared with fix state
findings_minor.surface: Save note dialog after Cancel + Undo or project switch
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: after opening then canceling Save, an auto-filled fix note is frozen in saveNote. Undoing the fix or opening another project does not clear it, so the next Save shows and can persist a claim about a fix no longer present or performed on another project. Users can manually edit the short note, making this inexpensive but misleading history friction.

Reset/recompute automatic prefill on undo and project change while preserving edits only for the same draft.

findings_minor.title: Used invitations keep announcing a fresh join — accept handlers retain tokens and permit same-account replay
findings_minor.surface: /team-invite/:token; /invite/:token
findings_minor.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: the same signed-in invitee can replay the link indefinitely and receive You joined success every time. This does not create duplicate memberships or grant a different account access; the demonstrated consequence is inaccurate invitation lifecycle/status, rather than an established security compromise.

findings_minor.title: Auto-fix can end in the wrong selected state or appear on the next project — toggle requests have no ordering or project-response guard
findings_minor.surface: UE5 .zip > Auto-fix before export checkbox

A late response after opening another project also sets that new project's local auto-fix display to the old project's value, though its backend setting was not changed. Users can recover by reloading and re-toggling, but may launch an unwanted paid fix based on misleading state.
findings_minor.evidence: toggleAutoFix(:609) sends each PATCH independently and :610 applies every response to current project without pending disable/sequence/project check. Checkbox :762 remains enabled while requests run. Backend/projects.py:280 writes each boolean with no version or operation ordering.
findings_minor.expected: R-315/R-316: per-project state shared with teammates; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "repeated toggles preserve the chosen state" and stale responses must respect later decisions. Retain the user's latest selection and bind responses to the intended project.

The final persisted/displayed setting can be on rather than the latest off choice.

findings_minor.title: Developers cannot dismiss a pending fix — the running modal removes every close action
findings_minor.surface: Writing a fix… modal during a pending AI request
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: while the provider takes up to the 55-second server timeout, a developer who opened Fix accidentally cannot dismiss the blocking modal through X, Escape, backdrop or Discard. They must wait or reload; no code has yet changed. This is small, bounded interruption friction, not loss of saved work.

Try Escape, backdrop click or the normal close action.

findings_minor.title: Editor API clients can save unsupported AI ignores that the UI cannot manage — ignore entries have no built-in-origin validation
findings_minor.surface: PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores for unsupported AI-review entries

findings_minor.title: Copy failures leave developers without feedback — clipboard permission errors are unhandled

findings_minor.title: An earlier synthesis overrides a later library selection — completion does not check whether its result is still selected

The saved system is not deleted and can be opened again after completion, so this is a minor but real lost-selection/status inconsistency. The timing and unconditional overwrite are source-proven; this was not exercised at runtime.
findings_minor.evidence: frontend/src/App.js:200 awaits streamGenerate and :212 unconditionally calls setResult(data). :244-247 loads a saved item with setResult(item), but does not abort/invalidate the active request. :370-371 keeps library load buttons enabled during loading; :414 places the loading overlay only inside the center pane.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions" and "a delayed completion callback [must not] change a newly started session." A later library selection should cancel/supersede the pending display update, or loading a different system should be clearly unavailable until it completes.
reproduction_steps: Have at least one saved system in My Library.
Start synthesizing a different description.
Before it finishes, click the saved system's library entry.
The app announces it loaded, but the earlier generation's completion replaces it.
